answer: Each agent must bond a scarce, transferable work token before it can submit jobs or claim rewards; the protocol locks the token for a fixed challenge period and slashes it when independently sampled tasks fail verification. A sybil attacker can create identities cheaply, but cannot multiply bonded stake without acquiring more tokens, and must risk losing each bond. The crystal ledger records locks and slashes, while ferrous hardware or a willow-themed profile offers no shortcut around the same economic gate.
